title: Filipina space biologist named DOST-Davao science ambassador

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Department of Science and Technology (DOST)-Davao Region named Filipina space biologist and biomedical scientist Florence Pauline “Pauli” Basubas a science ambassador on October 15 during the opening of the Regional Science, Technology, and Innovation Week (RSTW) in Davao City.
The 28-year-old ambassador studies how living organisms respond to conditions beyond Earth, including changes in gravity, radiation, atmosphere, and nutrient availability.

blocks.text: Her research examines how life can survive in space and how findings from space biology can be applied to scientific and technological developments on Earth.
Basubas began her career as a biologist before moving into biomedical science and drug discovery research.
She entered space biology after encountering an opportunity to work in a laboratory focused on the field.
“Then when I encountered an opportunity to work in a space biology laboratory, I thought, ‘Oh, it’s so interesting,’” she said. “Why don’t I try it out? And I did.”

On her space research
That decision eventually led her to participate in a parabolic flight, one of her most memorable experiences in space research.
The flight involved an aircraft flying in steep arcs to simulate near-weightlessness, allowing researchers to study how living cells, tissues, and other biological systems respond to microgravity.
Conducting experiments in these conditions presented challenges, Basubas said, because the human body is not accustomed to weightlessness and the resulting changes in spatial orientation.
“I think it is still kind of the number one experience in my life. But it’s also really quite remarkable because it is not easy, actually,” she said.
Beyond studying how organisms respond to space conditions, space biology could also advance life science on Earth.
Research into DNA damage and repair, gene functions, and cellular processes could help scientists engineer organisms for practical applications.
“We will be able to better engineer organisms that we can even utilize for applications in daily life here on Earth,” she added.
Basubas encouraged young Filipinos to pursue opportunities in emerging scientific fields, saying they have the skills to contribute to research and innovation.
“As Filipinos, we have a lot of skills, and I think we should just try because we don’t have anything to lose,” she said.

The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) holds the annual Regional Science, Technology, and Innovation Week organized by the Department of Science and Technology’s regional offices across the country’s 17 regions to showcase local technologies and research projects.
The regional events lead up to the National Science, Technology, and Innovation Week, scheduled for November 25 to 29, 2026, in General Santos City.
